title: unified-rollouts-proactive-shadow-canary-autorollback-workflow
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Adds proactive shadow-canary autorollback workflow and related observability and e2e tests. No customer-facing API changes. Backwards compatible rollout configs.
description:
Motivation: We need more proactive protection for model rollouts when exposing new model variants via shadow traffic and canary slices. Previous autorollback behavior only reacted to post-rollout telemetry; teams requested earlier detection and quarantine/probing of problematic variants before weight ramps. This PR implements a proactive shadow-canary autorollback workflow that integrates probing stages, composite metrics, and quarantine gates into the unified rollouts engine.

What this PR does: - Introduces a new 'proactive_shadow_canary' rollout workflow that places new variants into a shadow probing stage prior to traffic ramp. The stage runs short-lived probing traffic and validation checks (synthetic prompts, guardrail heuristics, and latency probes). - Adds composite metric support to the autorollback engine so policies can combine quality metrics (e.g., rouge/semantic-similarity regressions), latency, and error-rate signals with quorum thresholds. - Implements an automatic quarantine path: if probing fails the variant is quarantined (no ramp, alert to oncall, optional rollback). Quarantine can be manual-release or auto-unquarantine after specified fixes. - Enhances observability: new per-stage telemetry (probe_success_rate, probe_latency_p95, metric_quorum_vote), tracing tags for probing runs, and a timeline visualization in the Console to inspect probing history. - Adds e2e stability tests for the workflow and unit tests for the probing scheduler/metrics aggregator. - Small runtime changes to ensure KV cache warm-up for shadow probing requests and to avoid affecting production latency budgets.

Backward compatibility & safety: The new workflow is opt-in and does not change default rollout behavior. Existing canary/AB/shadow configurations remain supported. The autorollback engine retains its previous metric-driven rollback paths; composite metrics are additive and require explicit policy configuration.

Testing & validation: - Local unit tests for scheduler, aggregator, and policy matcher. - Integration tests simulating controlled regressions (quality drop, latency spike, error injection) to verify quarantine and auto-rollback behaviors. - End-to-end suite runs that exercise Console telemetry and stage timeline. - Load tests verified that shadow probing at configured probe rates adds <1% p95 latency impact to production pools in dedicated capacity.

Migration notes: No migration required for rollout objects; new workflow type available via rollout.spec.workflow = "proactive_shadow_canary". Console will show new timeline panels when the feature flag is enabled.

References: Linear tickets ENG-4321 (proactive probing workflow) and ENG-4380 (observability and e2e).

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Overall looks good. Two high-level asks: (1) make probe rate configurable per-variant and clearly bounded; (2) ensure we have a fallback to avoid double-instrumenting metrics in multi-region setups.
Priya Shah (author): Addressed probe rate configuration in rollout.spec.probe.rate and added multi-region guard in the scheduler. See commit feat: probe config + region guard.
María Rodriguez: Observability changes LGTM, but can we surface a single composite-score in the Console for quick triage?
Priya Shah: Added composite_score endpoint and a lightweight aggregated field to the timeline panel. Kept detailed signals available for advanced debugging.
Lin Zhao: Tests are comprehensive, unit coverage looks good. One nit: move the KV warm-up flag behind an experimental runtime flag so Dedicated customers can opt-in.
Priya Shah: Moved KV warm-up behind runtime.feature_flags.enable_probe_kv_warmup and added docs for Dedicated rollout.
